R1 R5 every fixture: the answer's decode equals the reference's decode of the original outside the cover, and is the cover colour inside it; the size is as displayed and `covered` counts the blocks or pixels the reference computed
R1 the cover is snapped outward, never inward: every pixel of every area is inside a covered rectangle, and the JPEG cover is whole MCUs
R1 an empty `areas` answers a copy with nothing covered: the whole decode equals the reference's

R2 a JPEG answer holds SOI, at most a bare JFIF APP0 or Adobe APP14, at most an EXIF APP1 with Orientation alone and no next IFD (no thumbnail), the tables, one frame, one scan, EOI, and nothing after

R2 the phone JPEG: its EXIF (make, GPS, sub-IFD), IFD1 thumbnail, XMP, ICC profile, comment, MPF index, the second image after EOI and the trailing bytes are all gone, and no byte run of any of them is in the answer

R2 a PNG answer holds IHDR, at most an eXIf with Orientation alone, the palette and transparency it needs, IDAT and IEND, and nothing after; the screenshot's text, XMP, EXIF, ICC, APNG frames and trailing bytes are gone
R3 every refusal by name, nothing answered but the refusal: each code is reached, and each answer is {ok:false, code, detail} alone
R6 pure: the same bytes and areas answer the same bytes, alone, repeated, or interleaved with other calls; the input is not changed
R7 no place is named in any refusal text or the module's exported words
R3 words: each refusal code's English is the design's row for it, read by word, never a sentence held here
R10 a 70-byte PNG declaring 30,000,000 x 1 RGBA is refused IMAGE_TOO_LARGE, by cover and by strip, naming the declared row and the bound, without the buffers it asked for
R10 a PNG row stride at the bound is judged as before, one byte over is IMAGE_TOO_LARGE (cover and strip), for each colour type
R10 a PNG of 1,000,000 empty IDAT chunks is refused IMAGE_TOO_LARGE by cover and strip; the bound's own count is processed as before
R10 a JPEG of 2,000,000 two-byte markers is refused IMAGE_TOO_LARGE by cover and strip; the bound's own count is judged as before
R10 a JP2 of more boxes than the bound, and a J2K codestream of more markers, are refused IMAGE_TOO_LARGE by strip
R10 the refusal is final: the same bytes answer the same refusal, and the code is declared with the others
R11 no numeric literal in the module's code is a ceiling it keeps: each ceiling is the table's figure and no file holds one of its own

R9 for every format, a progressive JPEG and an interlaced PNG among them: the reference decoder's pixels for the answer, as displayed, equal its pixels for the input (the hash Pillow gave the original)

R8 each format's answer holds only what R2 allows (no EXIF beyond the orientation, no thumbnail, XMP, ICC, comment, text, second image or bytes after the end), keeps what decides the decode, and carries the coded data byte for byte
R8 `changed` is false exactly when nothing was removed, and then the bytes equal the input; an answer stripped again is unchanged
R8 refusals by name, nothing answered but the refusal, and never a throw: each code is reached; damaged bytes of every fixture answer a copy or a named refusal
R6 R7 strip: the same bytes answer the same bytes, the input unchanged; no place in any refusal's words
